correctness.rationale: Exact conditioning on one chord gives crossing covariances; elementary random-matching pair probabilities give the matching additive covariance operator. Coefficient comparison proves projection onto every potential-edge indicator, not merely cyclic length counts. Fourth-power sums give Var(Q); the established crossing variance from Paguyo/Flajolet–Noy yields Var(residual)=n(n-2)/30 and sharp explained fraction. Pell reduction and positive Pell parametrization classify all zero cases. Exhaustive rational checks through n=7 and bounded Pell tests passed; no finite test is used to infer unrestricted validity.

value.rationale: It is structurally non-obvious that a single quadratic span moment explains a sharp fraction of variance of an intrinsically pairwise crossing count. The exact residual order n^2 versus total order n^3 establishes asymptotically complete linear predictability from chord lengths. Full edge-level optimality, a sharp universal 6/7 variance bound, and Pell-classified exceptional uncorrelated chord-length classes are natural exact probability questions, not arbitrary finite slices.
